policy.records: Only the round trips that lose something or warn about something. Everything this corpus can do that is absent from the list below is asserted to round trip clean, so a new loss fails by not being listed.
policy.reproduce: A row that stops reproducing fails too. That is deliberate: a fix should arrive with this file updated, so the shrinking of the suspected-defect list is a thing somebody can point at.
policy.states: documented - a limitation one of the conformance documents states. suspected-defect - a difference nobody decided on, which is what the CLI guide says round-tripping is actually good for. accepted - the normalized model's own behaviour, looked at and accepted.
policy.reviewer: A row is not classified by being written down. documented and accepted both need a reviewer and a date, and a documented row needs a reference to the document that states the limitation. CorpusBaselineGuardTests enforces it, the way PdfTestControlGuardTests does for the tool manifest.

roundTrips.why: Markdown has no way to express this and says so. markdown-conformance.md maps the writer property by property, and it reports markdown.paragraph-style or markdown.inline-style rather than dropping it silently. A paragraph aligns against a different one once its neighbour loses its leading spaces, so the comparison reports an insertion and a removal. A consequence of the row above rather than a separate finding. Leading and repeated spaces are structural in Markdown - indentation and code blocks are spelled with them - so a paragraph that begins with them cannot be written as ordinary text. The writer reports what it dropped from the style; the text itself is the format speaking.
roundTrips.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the writer-losses pass

roundTrips.why: The HTML writer embeds the picture as a data URI and says so (html.image.datauri); the reader does not turn a data URI back into a model image, so the placeholder character has nothing to attach to and goes. roundTrips.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the writer-losses pass

differences: text@p0: text differs: "Text around ￼ the image here." vs "Text around a generated square the image here."
roundTrips.why: An image does not survive a Markdown round trip, which markdown-conformance.md states and the writer reports (markdown.image.datauri). What it comes back as is now decided too: the reader recognizes the syntax and replaces it with the description CommonMark nominates as the fallback, reporting markdown.image.dropped. It used to leave the exclamation mark in the prose and report the loss as a dropped hyperlink, because `!` was not a character the inline parser knew.
roundTrips.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the Markdown image pass

differences: text@p0: text differs: "Text around ￼ the image here." vs "Text around  the image here."
roundTrips.why: The RTF writer emits the picture correctly, as a \pict destination carrying the PNG. The RTF *reader* skips it: rtf-conformance.md lists \pict among the skipped destinations and it is reported as rtf.embedded, which escalates to the shared capability code when a caller asks for embedded decoding. Both halves are covered by RtfWriterTests and RtfEmbeddedObjectReportTests. This row was previously recorded as a silent writer defect, which was wrong on every count - the baseline was filtering info diagnostics out, so the report it makes was invisible here.
roundTrips.reviewer: Claude Opus 5, on the writer-losses pass
